findings.problem: SensorWorkflow uses pub fields status: String, is_validated: bool, is_sent: bool which allow every combination including illegal ones (e.g. sent without validation, status='pending' with is_sent=true, status='sent' with sent_at_epoch_ms=None)
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can construct or mutate SensorWorkflow into an inconsistent state; the lifecycle invariant (validate -> send) is not enforced by the type system
findings.fix: Replace status, is_validated, is_sent with a SensorState enum (e.g. Pending, Validated, Sent) and make sent_at_epoch_ms part of the Sent variant. Remove pub fields and provide fallible constructors.

findings.problem: Three independent boolean/string fields encode a lifecycle but the compiler cannot prevent invalid transitions. mark_sent takes any SensorWorkflow and mutates it without checking preconditions.
findings.failure_mode: mark_sent can be called on a Pending or Unvalidated SensorWorkflow, producing a semantically invalid record with no error returned
findings.fix: Use an enum-based typestate or distinct newtypes (ValidatedSensorWorkflow, SentSensorWorkflow) so that mark_sent only accepts a Validated state and returns Sent via a fallible constructor.

findings.problem: Raw primitives (String, bool, Option<u64>) enter the domain struct directly with no parse boundary or smart constructor. There is no fallible constructor to validate or normalize input.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct invalid states directly by passing any String for status and any bool combination, bypassing all domain invariants
findings.fix: Add a fallible SensorWorkflow::try_from(...) or SensorWorkflow::new(...) that validates and returns a typed error. Replace String/bool/Option with domain types.

findings.problem: All fields of SensorWorkflow are pub, allowing external mutation of every lifecycle flag. mark_sent takes ownership and mutates status in-place rather than returning a new state.
findings.failure_mode: External code can mutate status, is_validated, is_sent arbitrarily without going through domain logic, breaking the lifecycle invariant at any point
findings.fix: Make all fields private (remove pub). Provide domain methods with proper signatures. Use the imperative shell for mutation; keep the core data inert.

findings.problem: mark_sent sets status to the magic string "sent". String-based state is fragile and error-prone — typos produce silent invalid states.
findings.failure_mode: A typo or mismatched string literal produces a sensor in a partially-sent state with no error. String comparison is required for state queries instead of enum match.
findings.fix: Replace status String with a SensorStatus enum (Pending, Validated, Sent) and use enum variants instead of string literals.

findings.problem: mark_sent has signature fn mark_sent(item: SensorWorkflow) -> SensorWorkflow with no error return type. It cannot reject invalid preconditions (e.g. not validated, already sent).
findings.failure_mode: The operation silently succeeds or corrupts state when preconditions are not met, violating the railway-oriented error handling principle
findings.fix: Return Result<SensorWorkflow, SensorError> (or use a typestate so the compiler enforces the precondition at the type level). Define a typed error enum for the domain.

findings.problem: mark_sent performs string allocation ("sent".to_string()) and in-place mutation. The pure domain logic is mixed with imperative mutation.
findings.failure_mode: Allocation on every mark_sent call; no separation between pure domain invariants and side-effectful mutation; not testable as a pure function
findings.fix: Use an enum for state (no allocation for status transition). Return a new struct with the updated state from a pure core function in the imperative shell.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is independent of is_sent. A sensor can be marked sent (is_sent=true) with sent_at_epoch_ms=None, or not sent with a timestamp present.
findings.failure_mode: Audit trails are incomplete — a sent sensor may lack its timestamp, or a pending sensor may have a future timestamp, making time-based queries and compliance checks unreliable
findings.fix: Tie the timestamp to the Sent state variant: use sent_at: u64 (non-Option) on the Sent variant of a SensorState enum, so a sent sensor always has a timestamp and a non-sent sensor never does.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw String with no domain identity semantics. No validation, no newtype, no guarantee of uniqueness or format.
findings.failure_mode: Empty strings, duplicates, or non-ASCII identifiers can enter the system. ID comparison is string-based rather than by domain identity.
findings.fix: Replace id: String with a SensorId newtype (e.g. pub struct SensorId(String)) and provide a fallible constructor with format validation at the parse boundary.

findings.problem: No [dev-dependencies], no [profile.test], no benchmark configuration, no test binary, no proptest/fuzz/Kani/Verus annotations. The crate has no verification infrastructure.
findings.failure_mode: No automated checks for undefined behavior, property-based correctness, bounded model checking, or formal refinement. Delivery has no evidence layer.
findings.fix: Add criterion for benchmarks, proptest for property testing, and Kani for bounded verification of the typestate transitions. At minimum, add a test binary.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for any performance claim
no profiler evidence (flamegraph, perf, or cargo flamegraph)
no allocation tracking (tracing-alloc, criterion allocation benchmark, or alloc counters)
no second-ring evidence (Kani proof harnesses, property tests, or fuzz targets)
no CLI/command harness or integration test binary
no formal verification (TLA+, Verus, or Kani) of the typestate machine
no test binary or unit tests for SensorWorkflow lifecycle
residual_risk: High. The domain model is entirely primitive-based with no type-level invariants. All lifecycle states are representable simultaneously. No tests, no benchmarks, no formal verification, and no evidence infrastructure exist. The code must be restructured with an enum-based typestate, fallible constructors, a typed error domain, and a parse boundary before any delivery.
